anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
gauntlet: gate=brainstorming/human-batch
Spec amendments: 2 need your call - from the spec review; applying as recommended reopens no tasks; no phase change.

1. Share retry policy - move retry policy into one owner. Adapters currently disagree about when to retry.
   Choosing which component owns retries is an architecture decision, so the reviewer left it to you.
   Example: adapter-local retry limits -> one coordinator retry limit
   Reviewer: changing retry ownership needs a human architecture choice
   Impact: retries: each adapter decides its own retry policy -> a single owner sets one retry policy for every adapter
   A) accept - a new retry service owns all retry policies
   B) alt-1 - the existing report coordinator owns the shared retry policy; adapters keep execution
   Custom: <your own answer> - executed as given; may redirect away from the spec
   Recommended: B - reusing the existing coordinator makes the policy consistent without adding a new service

2. Classify blocked execution - classify exit 126 as blocked rather than failed. Operators need to distinguish a launch problem from a report failure.
   This changes a status operators see, so the reviewer left the decision to you.
   Example: exit 126 = failed -> blocked
   Reviewer: operator-visible status changes need a human decision
   Impact: run status: a run exiting 126 reports as failed -> a run exiting 126 reports as blocked
   A) accept - exit 126 is reported as blocked
   Custom: <your own answer> - executed as given; may redirect away from the spec
   Recommended: A - a separate status lets operators tell launch failures apart from report failures

Reply with one line per item: `1. A`, `2. <your own text>`. Bare `1` takes every recommendation.
Standing grant: reply "auto-apply amends" - every later spec amendment in this flow (corrected facts, paths, verification lines, and scope, acceptance-criteria, or public-contract edits alike) applies without asking; only a redraw (changed problem statement, component added, removed, or re-bounded) still stops for you, and the grant never stands in for a spec approval.

Details
crosscut: Design / retries - old: each report adapter owns its retry policy -> new: a new retry service owns all retry policies
crosscut (alt-1): Design / retries - old: each report adapter owns its retry policy -> new: the existing report coordinator owns the shared retry policy; adapters keep execution
exit126: Design / run status - old: exit 126 is failed -> new: exit 126 is blocked

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved: both outputs open each numbered item with a what/why sentence, list A) accept and B) alt-1 with consequences, give lettered recommendations with reasons, use the `1. A` / bare `1` reply grammar without the legacy `<handle>=<choice>` form, and carry one human-call sentence per item. After rephrases the human-call sentence from "This is your call because ..." to "..., so the reviewer left it to you" - still satisfies f6, but the explicit "your call" phrasing in Before is the more robust anchor for a judge reading f6 literally, so keeping "This is your call because <reason>" costs nothing. Two small losses worth reverting even though no fact keys on them: After drops the concrete evidence (alpha retries twice, beta four) from item 1's opening sentence, and trims the Impact location from "Design / retries" / "Design / run status" to bare "retries" / "run status"; Before's fuller forms are closer to the batch's Location field. The split "crosscut" / "crosscut (alt-1)" Details lines are fine but Before's single `new (A) | new (B)` line is tighter and maps directly to the lettered options.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Nothing moved: both outputs open each item with a plain what/why sentence, list A) accept and B) alt-1 with one-line consequences, give `Recommended: B -` and `Recommended: A -` with reasons, carry one human-call sentence per item, and end with the `<n>. <letter or free text>` / bare `1` reply instruction with no legacy `<handle>=<choice>` form. The only After differences are outside the judged facts - the crosscut Impact line is now the option-neutral `adapter-owned policies -> one shared policy owner` rather than pre-committing to the coordinator, the Details line now shows `new (accept): ...` plus `Alternative alt-1: ...`, and the Recommended lines gained trailing periods. The Details rewrite is slightly at odds with the recommendation (it headlines accept as the `new` text while the menu recommends B); if you want to keep the neutral Impact wording, consider rendering Details as `old -> A: <accept text> / B: <alt-1 text>` or `new (recommended B): ...` so the summary and recommendation agree without reintroducing a pre-chosen option.
